I would say so long as they're working for -you- and not the other way around. In my job search I got approached by a lot of headhunters who wanted me to jump through hoops to get them their comission. At the end of the day they're hoping to bank off of -your- talent.
Did one ultimately help find your next position?
My current position no, but my previous one I had a recruiter call me up to schedule me for an interview that very phone call. And that one did work out.

Speaking as a candidate: A large percentage of the jobs in my sector are in the hands of recruiters, so I basically have to use them. So far only one has ever added any value to the process, and he wasn't really that good anyway.

Speaking as a hiring manager: No. They cost a shitload (as a rule of thumb placement fees are between 25% and 40% of the candidate's annual salary) and add absolutely nothing to the process. The only thing they do is screen and shortlist for me, but I can screen and shortlist 50 candidates in a day, and I certainly don't cost my company $25,000 to $40,000 per day, so its cheaper for me to do it myself. Also, I've seen recruiters screen out great candidates for bullshit reasons, which pisses me off to no end.
